title: Orderly Queue
summary: Given a string s and an integer k, select and move one of the first k characters to the end of s.
statement: Given a string s and an integer k, select and move one of the first k characters to the end of s. Determine the lexicographically smallest string achievable through any number of such operations.
constraints: Move one of the first k characters to the end repeatedly.
Return the lexicographically smallest reachable string.
hints: The reachable set changes completely at k=2.
For k=1 test every rotation; for k>1 sort.
Return min rotation when k==1, otherwise sorted characters.
A second selectable position permits adjacent-order rearrangement and hence every permutation.
editorial: A second selectable position permits adjacent-order rearrangement and hence every permutation.

tests.explanation: Only rotations are reachable; acb is smallest.
With k greater than one, any permutation is reachable, so aaabc is smallest.
